summary.headline: UTI AMC Q1 FY27 standalone core revenue flat YoY at Rs 308 crore, core PAT up 1% YoY to Rs 119 crore; dividend payout held above 95%.
summary.overview: Standalone core revenue (sale of services) was Rs 308 crore, flat YoY and up 1% QoQ, with core EBITDA of Rs 171 crore (up 1% YoY, 20% QoQ) and core PAT of Rs 119 crore (up 1% YoY, 72% QoQ). Consolidated core PAT rose 6% YoY to Rs 129 crore. Mutual fund average AUM reached Rs 3,92,691 crore, while PMS AUM fell Rs 3,16,000 crore QoQ after an EPFO mandate transfer. Management acknowledged weak investment performance in large schemes and flow market share below stock market share, with the call dominated by buyback, cost and subsidiary questions.

segments.name: Mutual fund (standalone)
segments.commentary: Average MF AUM Rs 3,92,691 crore; equity and passive ~70% of average MF AUM versus industry 62:38 equity to non-equity. Live folios 1.42 crore after adding 3.89 lakh; 2.51 lakh new PAN investors. Gross SIP inflows Rs 2,502 crore; SIP AUM Rs 45,595 crore, up 8.05% YoY.

segments.name: UTI Pension Fund (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4.31 lakh crore, up roughly 13% YoY from Rs 3.81 lakh crore; NPS industry share 24.16% versus 24.67% a year earlier. Management plans to more than double headcount over the next 12-18 months.

segments.name: UTI International
segments.commentary: AUM about USD 1.48 billion (Rs 14,027 crore) across 30+ countries; flagship India Dynamic Equity Fund (Ireland) at USD 511.56 million (Rs 4,839 crore). Management cited negative India sentiment and fund underperformance as reasons for negative flows.

segments.name: UTI Alternatives
segments.commentary: Total commitments of active funds Rs 3,843 crore versus about Rs 2,679 crore in June 2025. SDOF IV at about Rs 887 crore against planned Rs 1,500 crore plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe; MOF II at Rs 321 crore against planned Rs 1,000 crore plus Rs 1,000 crore greenshoe; SDOF IV commitments about Rs 900 crore.

guidance_outlook: Employee cost run rate guided at about Rs 95 crore per quarter standalone and about Rs 130 crore per quarter consolidated.
Other expenses for FY27 targeted at 8% to 10% increase over FY26 levels; no major IT or digital spend expected for the rest of the year beyond possible AI spend.
Dividend payout expected to stay above 95% of profit.
Mission 2031 target: scope to manage 2x current AUM; equity flow market share to be raised above stock market share.

Product pipeline for FY27 includes passive index/ETF launches (including UTI Nifty 500 ETF and UTI BSE Index Sector Leaders ETF) and, subject to approvals, a balanced hybrid fund and sectoral debt funds; SIF and GIFT City outbound funds planned for H2 FY27.
No employee cost guidance beyond FY27 given; management to revisit next year.
capex_capacity: Sales reorganisation complete post VRS: supervisory-to-field ratio at about 4 to 4.5, with branches clustered.
Pension subsidiary to significantly expand workforce over the next 18 months, with RMs, business development and sales roles, combining branches and field presence.
Standalone AMC headcount expected to stay flat; consolidated headcount rose to 1,512 from 1,435 in Q4 on subsidiary hiring.
International headcount expansion considered complete after US entry in 2024; future growth to be pursued through alliances rather than fixed cost bases.
demand_pricing: Industry average MF AUM Rs 84,18,486 crore in June 2026, up about 12.6% YoY; industry folios near 28 crore.

Yields: equity and hybrid about 72-73 bps; ETF and index about 8 bps; cash and arbitrage about 12 bps; fixed income about 20 bps. Management said the 5 bps TER/exit-load change was passed on to intermediaries with no margin dilution.
Large & mid-cap fund drawing strongest net inflows, with share of industry net sales at about 3% to 3.5% per month; flexi cap saw net redemptions but rising SIP pipeline.
Hybrid (aggressive hybrid) share of industry net sales about 2% to 3%.
Index fund inflows described as significantly retail and significantly positive; no EPFO contribution commented on.
SIP registrations in the 18-25 age group rose 18.6% QoQ to 98,127; 26-40 cohort new SIPs up 6.8% and new clients up 11.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the 5 bps TER/exit load change on yields and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Lakhotia said there is no margin dilution; the TER impact was fully passed on to intermediaries, as reflected in stable yields.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the non-controlling interest line zero, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Lakhotia said SDOF II had returned its money and SDOF III had partly been sold, so consolidation was not required this quarter. Payout is expected to stay above 95% of profit.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback given cash of about 40% of market cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Vetri Subramaniam said a buyback is not on the table; payout is already 95% to 100%, and the focus is growing market cap.

qa_highlights.question: Flexi cap outflows and other large-scheme flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Lakhotia said flexi cap had net redemptions but gross sales and SIPs were encouraging; large & mid-cap had strong net inflows.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the international business after two to three quarters of pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Subramaniam attributed negative flows to weak India sentiment and fund underperformance over two years, called it cyclical, and said growth will come via alliances.

qa_highlights.question: Rising employee count QoQ and the ROI on pension and international investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the standalone AMC headcount is stable; the increase is in pension and alternatives. Pension growth is funded without a profitability dent, and international headcount is not expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Market share loss and NFO plans for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Samsi listed passive and active launches, with SIF and GIFT City outbound funds in H2. Subramaniam said market share loss reflects redemptions in large schemes and will turn only with performance recovery.

qa_highlights.question: M&A optionality and whether UTI is in talks?
qa_highlights.answer: Subramaniam said the company keeps a cash buffer for possible bolt-on acquisitions in AMC, alternatives or international, but there are no active talks.

risks_watch: Flow market share in equity remains below stock market share; large-scheme redemptions and weak investment performance persist, with management admitting execution gaps in investment excellence.
International AUM and flows negative for about two years; P&L volatility from seed capital.
PMS AUM fell Rs 3,16,000 crore QoQ after the EPFO mandate transfer; fee impact described as marginal.
Cost growth beyond FY27 not guided; management to revisit next year, and industry competition could push costs up.
Pension headcount to more than double, which could weigh on consolidated costs despite management saying there is no profitability dent.
Capital allocation: large cash balance (about 40% of market cap per analyst) with buyback ruled out and M&A optionality cited.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise scale, digital and pension growth, and cost discipline, but candid and cautious on investment performance, international flows and equity flow market share. Management avoided committing on buyback or cost guidance beyond FY27.
key_quotes: We are not interested in trying to exploit operating leverage.
So, the guidance on the employee cost that we gave earlier was Rs 95 crores for the standalone entity and close to around Rs 130 crores per quarter for a consolidated entity.
Investment performance is where, we are not where we would like to be, in my opening remarks I made the call investment excellence, and we've not managed to execute well on that.
No, there's no proposal that we are considering at this point of time. It's not on the table.
